It never ends - in 20 years your outlook is likely to be completely different on just about everything you now know. Don't worry about that too much... it's part of the deal.

A few Pro tips:

Take care of your health - seriously, learn about nutrition, and exercise, and become that - because in about 15 years you will start to slow down - and by the time you reach 50 you will have half of your energy - and your friends start dying off of age related stuff. You can live to be 80 with the help of modern medicine, but life isn't a lot of fun if you spend the later half of it as a cripple. Do the health thing now, and enjoy decades of disease free existence.

Err on the side of caution - because in the long run you will find you are just as likely to have been wrong as right.

People change - it happens - sometimes they develop an entirely new personality, seemingly overnight - best not to be too dependent upon others if you can avoid that. You will be betrayed, so don't be surprised, hedge accordingly. This includes people you have known well for decades. Very few people you will ever meet are actually capable of keeping their word. People who can and do are rare indeed.

Acquire some self employable skills - learn to be able to obtain work on the side for yourself when you need it. Having a good job is great if you can get one, but any job can be lost at any time, for any reason. You should always assume that you might lose the job tomorrow, and that it might take a long time to find another decent one. If you have skills that you can use to earn money between jobs, you will be much better off. Practical stuff, like painting, drywall, carpentry, electrician, plumbing, bar tending, etc - you can almost always find temporary work doing something like this no matter how bad the economy gets.

Learn to fly below the radar. You'll probably live a lot longer if people are not shooting at you - so use the terrain for cover and generally move so as not to be overly noticed. Learn this concept and you can for the most part do whatever you want. The people who fly high are also the ones who attract the most flak. Out of sight = out of mind. Nobody pays much attention to Joe Schmoe.

Work towards becoming independent of the system - many people have found when it is time to collect the pension, the pension is gone. The system is constantly changing, and promises made today may no longer exist when the time comes to collect. Better to set yourself up so you are not reliant on these mechanisms of modern society - to the greatest degree possible.

I'll wrap this up with a final mention - you are human, and it is in your nature to fuck up. Sooner or later you will probably do so big time. It happens to everybody. The thing about that is you need to learn from it, then forgive yourself, and move on. Do not carry the burdens of your failures throughout your life. You are supposed to have failures, and successes. No matter how bad things are, or have been in the past, there is no saying how things can be tomorrow, and your entire situation can change overnight. You can miss out on seizing good opportunities if your mind is bogged down in the past. Live in this moment, and tomorrow is always a new day.
